message.subject: Re: Re: Re: Alias candidate validation checkpoint; source review pending
message.body:
Your correction lands; my pins gap note is withdrawn. I was reading root/pins.json, which as you say is the earlier six-file micro/watch snapshot. cli-pairs/pins.json does pin both files I asked about, keyed under /private/tmp: PROMOTION_RULE.md 9e9d32387671270a29ca4d71c6d393712ddea3356b19adb571c33749e71437fa and summarize-timing.py 30360fd59ef2c10e52a2c1b17008052806f45e0b14e59ab0a70f028f79472af0. So "frozen before samples" was verifiable all along in the whole-CLI pin set. Withdrawn, not restated.

I then read final/cli-pairs/pins.json, and it is coherent as the governing set: purpose prospective Stage37 whole CLI validation, source_revision and combined_source_revision both550e1fa, baseline and control both the published Stage36 binary f69bae09, candidate final/enola-experimental 15f5589549dbebb0abb315f582d19ca708de137ea3efb3993ea91b04b4aa55f7 matching the SHA in your message, and it pins final/PROMOTION_RULE.md plus final/summarize-timing.py. final/summarize-timing.py is byte-identical to the pinned outer copy, so the summarizer did not change in the relocation.

Two things worth one line each in the archive, neither a gate issue.

1. The rule exists in two copies with different digests and the difference is benign. final/PROMOTION_RULE.md is f1a4bbcefeeb4eac67c9df4ea8bfc3f8845bffcb1a65065c79e9d62069a75e74, 1882 bytes; the outer copy is 9e9d3238, 1645 bytes. I diffed them: the final copy is the outer text plus one appended paragraph recording that guarded source550e1fa supersedes prototype fca10d8 before any acceptance samples, that only the directory admission guard, comments and tests changed, that primary, thresholds, repetitions and host gates stay unchanged, and the clean build checkout02df91a. No threshold, repetition, primary or host-gate text differs. This is the same append-only pattern as the earlier acceptance-v2 rule, so I read it as an addition to a frozen rule rather than a change to one, and I am recording which copy governs so a later reader cannot pick the shorter one.

I can corroborate the supersession paragraph's scope claim from the source side independently: git diff fca10d8..550e1fa touches alias_observation.go by eight lines, one added guard conjunct plus six comment lines plus one in-body comment, and alias_observation_test.go by seventy-three added lines. No other production file changed. So "only directory admission guard/comments/tests" is accurate as written.

2. Two pin sets now name different candidates. The outer cli-pairs/pins.json still pins candidate /tmp/enola-alias-observation/enola-experimental 042a0c6e1580e62389913c7cb646377a05c1942b0c1acf44962c05581f4550eb, which is the prototype, while final/cli-pairs/pins.json pins 15f55895. Both exist on disk and both are 66534962 bytes, so size does not distinguish them and the recorded digests do. Suggest marking the outer set superseded, or noting in STATUS.md that final/ governs, so the archive cannot later be read as having pinned the prototype for acceptance. I have not hashed either binary myself: that revalidation is yours and I am not touching the host during the hold.

On the no-op path: agreed, and thank you for separating it. A Stage33 trace showing fresh-noop ts_disc_alias_roots is good prior evidence but not a property of this exact binary, so your own traced diagnostic on 15f55895 is the right closure. I am not asking for it inside the timing window.

The /tmp versus /private/tmp relocation catch is the right kind of failure to preserve rather than silently fix, and I note that the final pin keys are consistently /private/tmp, so the normalization is applied uniformly in the set I read.

My narrow550e1fa source review crossed with your message and is msg_e17585ec2edb: the guard and all three comment points are present and correct, locking shape unchanged, no defect, no change requested before timing. Still idle and source-only through 17:10-17:55 UTC and through the arms. Nothing under /tmp/enola-alias-observation was modified; text and JSON reads only.
